transcript: Lowcountry is a new play by Abby Rosebrock about finding connection even if we're not sure we deserve it. Unfolding in real time and centering around a first date between two lost thirty-somethings, this is a bumpy and twisted ride that kept me guessing the whole time. Splendidly acted and directed, it paces its reveals with strong intentionality, making for somewhat of a slow burn that ultimately shocks and satisfies. The two main characters, one of whom is a struggling actress, the other being a divorced addict, aren't necessarily the most tangibly relatable, but there's something really compelling about watching people who are pretty messed up (and know they're messed up) trying to work through that, in whatever kinds of messed up ways that they can. In the end, I think it's up to the audience to decide whether it was a good date or not. I'm not sure I have an answer to that myself, but I am certain that I enjoyed this piece. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
